judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core insuring promise is short and its operative condition, that the insured 'died while the contract was in force', is a phrase whose boundary depends on other machinery rather than on itself. Nothing internal names an ambiguous term beyond the badly reproduced text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a bare state list with no operative sentence at all, so the right it confers cannot be determined from the provision itself. A truncated enumeration is the paradigm of an unusable list-scope provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The state lists across c003-c006 are supposed to partition coverage but overlap incompletely with the generic 20-day right in c002, leaving unclear which window governs a given policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the flat 20-day right in c002 and against the different 45-day PA rule in c006, and 'replacement' is nowhere defined elsewhere in the contract.
